note: RVV optimization catalogue for CPU kernel campaigns. Statuses are NOT recorded here: the search tree records what was tried, under which parent, with what outcome. `detect` is a Python expression over a static profile (portforge_tt/cpu/profile.py): loops (number of hot loops), max_lmul, widest_sew, calls (list), mnemonics (set of hot-loop mnemonics), counts (summed per class), vsetvl_per_iter, spills, moves. `x280` notes are measured on the board (portforge_tt/cpu/data/x280-calib.json). `kind: fix` marks techniques whose detect means the problem is absent; the policy does not offer them to a parent whose code already satisfies it.

sources.rvv-guide: portforge_tt/guides/RVV_GUIDE.md (this repo, from the 2026-10 xnnpack-rvv campaigns)
sources.saltyrn-survey: SALTyRN optimized kernels on the X280 (2026-10-18 survey, memory rvv-smoke-findings)

categories.config: vector configuration: SEW, LMUL, vsetvl placement
categories.isel: instruction selection: cheaper or fused instructions for the same math
categories.algorithm: change the arithmetic itself while staying bit-exact
categories.memory: how data moves between memory and registers
categories.loop: loop structure: strip-mining, unrolling, pipelining, hoisting
categories.scalar: the scalar side: prologue, bookkeeping, calls
categories.offload: north star: work moved to other engines on the same card

techniques.title: One vsetvl-driven loop; the tail is a smaller vl
techniques.mechanism: Replace a fixed-width main loop plus scalar tail with one loop whose vl comes from the remaining count.
techniques.helps_when: Ported from Neon/SSE with a scalar tail; small batches dominated by tail code.
preconditions: batch is in bytes for many XNNPACK families: divide by element size once

failure_modes: off-by-one vl at the last iteration

techniques.x280: baseline structure of every merged RVV kernel

prior.basis: only helps if the source had a scalar tail

techniques.title: Raise LMUL until the widest stage is m8
techniques.mechanism: Larger register groups mean fewer instructions per element and longer chimes that hide latency.
techniques.helps_when: The hot loop runs at LMUL <= 2 and has no spills; latency-bound chains (mul, fixed-point) at small LMUL.
preconditions: widest stage of a widening chain must stay within m8

failure_modes: register-group alignment errors at compile time

techniques.detect: max_lmul is not None and max_lmul >= 4
techniques.x280: ALU cost is 2 cycles per LMUL (DLEN 256) so throughput per element is flat, but latency (add 3, mul 7 cycles at m1/m2) is hidden only from m4 up

prior.basis: u1v->u4v gaps in XNNPACK benches; calib latency table

techniques.title: Do the arithmetic at the narrowest exact width
techniques.mechanism: Prove a bound on every intermediate and run the chain at e16 instead of e32 (or e8 instead of e16): half the register groups, half the cycles per element.
techniques.helps_when: A widening chain goes to i32 but the values provably fit i16 for the whole producer domain.
preconditions: range proof over the init's whole output domain (not the test values)
intermediate products and sums, not only inputs

failure_modes: overflow at parameter extremes (SALTyRN qs8-vcvt: (int16)(m<<7) at m>=256)

techniques.detect: widest_sew is not None and widest_sew <= 16
techniques.x280: cost per instruction is per LMUL, so halving SEW at fixed element count halves LMUL and the cycles

prior.basis: qs8-vcvt pf1 (i16 chain = u4v), v1 i32 chain was 0.50x

techniques.title: Dispatch on runtime parameters to the cheapest exact path
techniques.mechanism: Check scalar parameter predicates once per call and run a loop specialized for that regime (fewer ops where the math simplifies), keeping a general path.
techniques.helps_when: The formula collapses for common parameter values (multiplier a power of two, unit scale, zero offsets).
preconditions: each predicate must make its path exact on the regime's whole domain
dispatch is by proven predicate, never by special-casing test values
regimes complete and disjoint over the init's range

failure_modes: off-by-one predicate boundary (an SMT-config gate missed one for vcvt pf2)

techniques.x280: branches before the loop cost a few cycles; libgcc calls in the predicate (ctz without Zbb) cost ~18% at batch 256

prior.basis: qs8-vcvt pf2: 1.18x bench, 4.5x m=256, 0.82x at batch 256 in D1 from a __ctzdi2 call

techniques.title: Collapse a regime to one saturating op
techniques.mechanism: When the requantization is an exact shift by zero (m == 256 in qs8-vcvt), the whole chain is one e8 saturating add/subtract of a scalar.
techniques.helps_when: A regime where multiplier and shift cancel; usually the identity/default quantization.
preconditions: the scalar operand fits the narrow element type, else a widened path
techniques.x280: a 3-instruction loop is memory-bound at 32 B/cycle in L1

prior.basis: qs8-vcvt pf2 regime A: 4.5x at 16k elements

techniques.title: Fold zero points and rounding into one scalar bias
techniques.mechanism: Move every per-call constant (zero points times multipliers, output zero point shifted, rounding constant) into a scalar computed once, so the loop does mul + add + narrow.
techniques.helps_when: Requantization with zero points applied per element.
preconditions: the folded bias must not overflow its type for any producer parameters (SALTyRN qs8-vadd: ozp<<shift wraps int32 at shift 30)
do not re-add a term the init already folded (SALTyRN qu8-vadd)
techniques.x280: removes one ALU op per element: ~20% of a 5-op chain

techniques.title: Use vnclip for shift + round + saturate + narrow
techniques.mechanism: One vnclip with the right vxrm replaces separate rounding shift, clamp and narrow.
techniques.helps_when: A requantization tail shifts, saturates and narrows.
preconditions: rounding mode must match the scalar kernel's (round-half-up is RNU)
techniques.x280: vnclip costs 4 cycles per LMUL of the destination (reads a 2x source)

prior.basis: autocomp menu; used by every fast requant kernel

techniques.title: Scalar-operand forms (.vx/.vi/.vf) for broadcast parameters
techniques.mechanism: Use the scalar register operand instead of splatting a parameter into a vector register.
techniques.helps_when: The loop holds splatted constants that cost registers (forcing lower LMUL) or a vmv.v.x per iteration.
preconditions: scalar operand fits the element width (vx sign-extends from XLEN; .vi is 5-bit)
techniques.x280: same cost as .vv; the win is register pressure

techniques.title: vmacc/vmadd (and vwmacc) instead of vmul + vadd
techniques.mechanism: One multiply-accumulate replaces two ALU ops.
techniques.helps_when: A multiply is immediately followed by an add of a vector or broadcast value.
preconditions: integer: exact; float: vfmacc is fused - only if the reference is fused too (Neon vmlaq is not)

failure_modes: float fused vs unfused ulp differences

techniques.x280: vmacc throughput equals vadd (2 cycles per LMUL), so one op saved is a full op

techniques.title: Widening arithmetic instead of extend + op
techniques.mechanism: vwadd/vwsub/vwmul widen as part of the arithmetic, saving a separate vsext/vzext.
techniques.helps_when: The loop extends an input and then immediately adds/subtracts/multiplies it.
techniques.x280: vwadd costs the same as vsext at the source LMUL

techniques.title: Fewer vsetvli per iteration; group same-vtype ops
techniques.mechanism: Order instructions so ops sharing SEW/LMUL are adjacent; set vtype once per stage.
techniques.helps_when: The static profile shows more vsetvli per iteration than distinct stages.

failure_modes: using a stale vl after a vtype change

techniques.x280: a vtype-changing vsetvli costs ~1 cycle, small next to 8-16 cycle m4/m8 ops

techniques.title: Avoid vmv<n>r copies in the hot loop
techniques.mechanism: Structure data flow so values are produced in the register group that consumes them.
techniques.helps_when: The profile shows vmv1r/2r/4r/8r inside the loop (load-ahead pipelining often introduces them).
techniques.x280: a vmv4r costs ~8 cycles: load-ahead's copy made it 0.97x

techniques.title: Software-pipeline the next load
techniques.mechanism: Issue the next iteration's load before this iteration's compute so memory latency overlaps.
techniques.helps_when: Memory latency is exposed (L2/DRAM working sets) and the loop is short.
preconditions: must not read past XNN_OOB_READS slack
techniques.x280: rejected on qs8-vcvt in L1 (0.97x): the vector unit is decoupled already

techniques.title: Unroll with several independent accumulators
techniques.mechanism: Split a loop-carried dependence (reductions, running max) across accumulators to hide latency.
techniques.helps_when: Reductions or running extrema at LMUL <= 2 where latency (7 cycles for mul) is exposed.
preconditions: integer only, or float when the reference order is not part of the contract
techniques.x280: at m4/m8 latency is already hidden, so extra accumulators mostly add register pressure

techniques.title: Element-wise accumulate in the loop, reduce once at the end
techniques.mechanism: Keep a vector accumulator with vadd in the loop and do one vredsum after it.
techniques.helps_when: A reduction calls vredsum (or similar) every iteration.
preconditions: accumulator width must not overflow over the longest batch
techniques.x280: vredsum costs 29-67 cycles vs 2-16 for vadd

prior.basis: calibration: reductions are 4-20x an ALU op

techniques.title: Slides or segment loads instead of vrgather
techniques.mechanism: Replace arbitrary register permutations with vslide or vlseg/vsseg for regular patterns.
techniques.helps_when: The profile shows vrgather/vcompress in the hot loop.

verifier_support.note: segment-tuple types (vuint32m2x4_t) have no SALTyRN shims

techniques.detect: counts.get('permute', 0) == 0 or not any(m.startswith('vrgather') for m in mnemonics)
techniques.x280: vrgather is element-serial: 68 cycles at e8m1 (64 elements), 516 at e8m8

techniques.title: If a gather is unavoidable, run it at LMUL 1
techniques.mechanism: Split a high-LMUL vrgather into LMUL=1 gathers; cost grows with the table size per instruction.
techniques.helps_when: Lookup-table kernels (vrgather as LUT) at LMUL >= 2.
preconditions: the table fits one register (VLEN/8 bytes at e8)
techniques.x280: measured gather cost doubles per LMUL step (68/132/260/516 cycles at e8)

techniques.title: Unit-stride segment loads/stores for interleaved data
techniques.mechanism: vlseg<nf>/vsseg<nf> de-interleave AoS to SoA in one instruction instead of strided loads.
techniques.helps_when: Interleaved layouts: complex numbers (vcmul), channels (packw), transposes.

verifier_support.note: tuple types are not shimmed: gate with the exact check

techniques.x280: e32, VLEN 512, L1, 128-byte stride: strided segment loads vlsseg2/4/8 at m1 take 17/19/32 cycles (about one segment per cycle up to nf=4: 4 elements/cycle at nf=8); unit-stride vlseg2 m1 5 cycles, vlseg4 19, vlseg8 32

techniques.title: Prefer unit-stride over strided or indexed memory ops
techniques.mechanism: Re-layout or block the loop so the vector unit reads contiguous memory.
techniques.helps_when: vlse/vsse or vluxei in the hot loop.
techniques.detect: not any(m.startswith(('vlse', 'vsse', 'vluxei', 'vloxei', 'vsuxei', 'vsoxei')) for m in mnemonics)
techniques.x280: measured: vlse32 is 1 element/cycle (16 cycles at m1, 64 at m4), vsse32 0.5 element/cycle (32 at m1), indexed vluxei32/vsuxei32 about 2 cycles per element; unit vle32/vse32 cost 5 cycles at m1-m2 and 8 at m4 (32 B/cycle)

techniques.title: Tail/mask agnostic policies (ta, ma)
techniques.mechanism: Use _ta/_ma intrinsics so destinations need not be read; undisturbed policies add a dependency.
techniques.helps_when: The kernel uses _tu/_mu intrinsics without needing the old values.
preconditions: only when the tail/masked-off lanes are never stored

failure_modes: garbage in lanes that are later stored

verifier_support.note: _tu/_mu variants have NO shims: using them forfeits the SMT gate

techniques.x280: not yet calibrated

techniques.title: Restrict work with vl instead of masks
techniques.mechanism: When only leading elements are active, shorten vl rather than computing and masking all lanes.
techniques.helps_when: A mask selects a prefix of the vector.
techniques.x280: not yet calibrated

techniques.title: vmerge or arithmetic masks instead of data-dependent branches
techniques.mechanism: Compute both sides and select with vmerge, or fold the selection into arithmetic (and/xor for lrelu).
techniques.helps_when: Per-element conditions such as leaky-relu slopes, clamps, argmax updates.
preconditions: NaN/±0 behaviour must match the scalar compare (vfmax differs from compare+select)
techniques.x280: vmerge costs like vadd

techniques.title: Explicit compare+select where the reference does, not vfmin/vfmax
techniques.mechanism: Mirror the scalar kernel's comparisons so NaN and ±0 results match bit for bit.
techniques.helps_when: Float min/max/argmax/clamp kernels.
techniques.x280: same cost class as vfmax

techniques.title: No libgcc calls in the prologue or loop
techniques.mechanism: Replace __ctzdi2/__clzdi2/__divdi3-style calls with arithmetic the target has (XNNPACK compiles RVV with -march=rv64gcv: no Zbb), or with a vector equivalent, or precompute in the init.
techniques.helps_when: The static profile lists calls; small batches dominate.
techniques.x280: pf2's __ctzdi2 call cost ~18% at batch 256

techniques.title: Hoist loop-invariant work and splats out of the loop
techniques.mechanism: Compute splats, rounding constants and derived scalars once before the loop.
techniques.helps_when: vmv.v.x or scalar recomputation inside the hot loop.
techniques.x280: scalar work overlaps with the decoupled vector unit; vector splats cost a full op

techniques.title: Fewer, wider stores; no stores of intermediates
techniques.mechanism: Keep intermediates in registers; store once per output element at the narrowest type.
techniques.helps_when: The loop writes intermediates or stores at a wider type than needed.
techniques.x280: L1 stores 32 B/cycle; L2 copy only ~2.6 B/cycle

prior.basis: SALTyRN survey: wins came from wider stages and fewer stores

techniques.title: Pick unroll/LMUL from vlenb at runtime
techniques.mechanism: Choose among compiled variants once per process from the actual VLEN, instead of a compile-time choice.
techniques.helps_when: A family's best variant differs between VLEN 128 and 512/1024 (check QEMU instruction counts and the board).
preconditions: purely a speed choice: every variant must be exact
techniques.x280: only VLEN 512 can be timed here

techniques.title: North star: offload a bulk stage to the Tensix cores on the same Blackhole
techniques.mechanism: The X280 drives control flow; a dense, regular stage (GEMM-like, stencil, LUT over large batches) runs on Tensix cores reached over the NoC, if the round trip amortizes.
techniques.helps_when: Large batches of BF16-friendly dense work; never for tiny calls.
preconditions: TT-Metal and tt-bh-linux must coexist on the card (unverified)
end-to-end time including the round trip must beat RVV

failure_modes: BF16/SFPU numerics differ from the CPU reference

techniques.x280: no published X280<->Tensix work; spike in research/tt-offload first

techniques.title: Strided segment stores instead of strided segment loads
techniques.mechanism: vssseg<nf> writes nf consecutive fields per segment at a byte stride. A 2-D reorder (transpose, packing) can load contiguous rows with unit-stride vle and scatter them with one strided segment store, instead of gathering with vlsseg and storing unit-stride.
techniques.helps_when: Data movement kernels whose gather side uses strided or strided-segment loads (x32-transposec, packw).
preconditions: nf * LMUL <= 8
output segments (nf consecutive elements) are contiguous in the destination

failure_modes: writes into row padding past block_height

verifier_support.smt: no shim for tuple intrinsics (exact check only)

techniques.x280: measured e32, VLEN 512, L1: vssseg2/4/8 at m1 = 16 cycles whatever nf (one segment per cycle: 8 elements/cycle at nf=8), twice the rate of vlsseg8 (32 cycles); vssseg2 m4 64 cycles; unit vle32 m4 loads 64 elements in 8 cycles

techniques.title: Walk large 2-D blocks in cache-sized sub-blocks
techniques.mechanism: When one call covers a block larger than L1, iterate over sub-blocks sized so every input and output cache line touched is reused before eviction, instead of streaming whole column strips.
techniques.helps_when: Large single calls (transposes, packing) where measured cycles per element jump at sizes beyond L1/L2, especially with power-of-two strides that alias cache sets.
preconditions: results do not depend on traversal order (pure data movement or independent outputs)

failure_modes: edge sub-blocks skipped or done twice

techniques.x280: L1 D 32 KiB-class working set (32 B/cycle), L2 ~13 B/cycle, DRAM ~0.7 B/cycle; upstream x32 transposes run 13-14 cycles/element on 1024x1024 (4096-byte strides) vs ~1 cycle/element at 256x256
